failures.claim: IFRS S1 permits information required by an IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standard to be included in sustainability-related financial disclosures by cross-reference to another report published by the entity, subject to requirements in paragraphs B45–B47.
The entity uses cross-referencing only when the conditions in paragraphs B45–B47 are met.

warnings.claim: IFRS S1 requires a complete set of sustainability-related financial disclosures to present fairly all sustainability-related risks and opportunities that could reasonably be expected to affect the entity’s prospects.
The entity identifies sustainability-related risks and opportunities using the application guidance in paragraphs B1–B12.
The entity discloses information that is relevant and faithfully represented, including ensuring the depiction is complete, neutral and accurate.
The entity prepares disclosures to be comparable, verifiable, timely and understandable.
IFRS S1 requires disclosure of material information about sustainability-related risks and opportunities that could reasonably be expected to affect the entity’s prospects.
The entity identifies and discloses material information using the application guidance in paragraphs B13–B37.
IFRS S1 requires the sustainability-related financial disclosures to be for the same reporting entity as the related financial statements.
The entity prepares sustainability-related financial disclosures for the same reporting entity as the related financial statements.

IFRS S1 requires an entity to provide information in a manner that enables users to understand connections between the items to which the information relates, including connections between sustainability-related risks and opportunities.

IFRS S1 requires an entity to provide information enabling users to understand connections between disclosures within the sustainability-related financial disclosures, including governance, strategy, risk management, and metrics and targets.

IFRS S1 requires an entity to provide information enabling users to understand connections across the sustainability-related financial disclosures and other general purpose financial reports published by the entity, such as the related financial statements.
The entity identifies the financial statements to which these sustainability-related financial disclosures relate.
When currency is specified as the unit of measure in sustainability-related financial disclosures, the entity uses the presentation currency of the related financial statements.
Unless another IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standard permits or requires otherwise, IFRS S1 requires disclosures about governance, strategy, risk management, and metrics and targets.

The entity presents its sustainability-related financial disclosures under the four pillars (governance, strategy, risk management, metrics and targets) and links related information across the report to support connected information.

IFRS S1 requires an entity, in identifying sustainability-related risks and opportunities that could reasonably be expected to affect the entity’s prospects, to apply IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards.

IFRS S1 requires an entity to refer to and consider the applicability of the disclosure topics in the SASB Standards and permits concluding those topics are not applicable in the entity’s circumstances.

IFRS S1 requires that, in identifying applicable disclosure requirements about a sustainability-related risk or opportunity, an entity applies the IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standard that specifically applies to that risk or opportunity.

When no IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standard specifically applies to a sustainability-related risk or opportunity, IFRS S1 requires an entity to use judgement to identify information that is relevant to users’ decision-making and faithfully represents the risk or opportunity.

In making the judgement when no specific IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standard applies, IFRS S1 requires an entity to refer to and consider the applicability of the metrics associated with the disclosure topics included in the SASB Standards and permits concluding those metrics are not applicable in the entity’s circumstances.

IFRS S1 permits information required by an IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standard to be included in sustainability-related financial disclosures by cross-reference to another report published by the entity, subject to requirements in paragraphs B45–B47.
The entity uses cross-referencing only when the conditions in paragraphs B45–B47 are met.
